title: Getting started
summary: From a new project to your first chapter
lead: A project is a workspace that keeps one story's chapters, setting documents, notes and the relationships between them in one place. Creating a project opens its workspace right away, and everything you write saves automatically.

sections.title: Create a project
sections.body:
Select New project at the top right of your project list. If you have no projects yet, select Create your first project in the middle of the page.

- The project title is required and can be up to 255 characters.
- The description is optional and can be up to 500 characters.
- Select Create project and the new workspace opens right away.

sections.title: Work with project cards
sections.body:
Select a card to open its workspace. Each card shows the description, the file you last worked on and when you last worked on it.

Open a card's more menu (⋯) and choose Edit to change its name and description, or Move to trash to move the project to the trash. A project in the trash keeps its files and settings and can be restored.

sections.title: Find your way around
sections.body:
The sidebar on the left holds, from top to bottom:

- The account menu and project switcher: jump to another project or back to your project list.
- Search · Relationship map · Timeline · Notes: views across the whole project.
- Refresh setting docs: finds new details and relationships in your chapters and proposes them.
- Setting check: the AI finds where a chapter contradicts your setting documents or earlier chapters.
- Favorites: the documents you open most.
- Files: chapters and setting documents, grouped in category folders.
- Import · Trash · Settings · Help

Select Tour the workspace in Help to see the guided tour of the screen again.

sections.title: Write your first chapter
sections.body:
In the Files area, open the more menu (⋯) of the Manuscript folder and choose Add manuscript. Type a name and press Enter; the chapter is created and opens. You can also select Manuscript under Create new on a new tab.

Your text saves 0.8 seconds after you stop typing, and at least every 5 seconds while you keep going. When the status at the right of the toolbar reads Saved, it is saved. Press ⌘S (Ctrl+S on Windows) to save right away.

sections.title: Replay the intro
sections.body: Open Guide on the left of your project list and select Replay the intro at the top to see the introduction you saw when you signed up. On its last step you can also create the sample project ‘The Glass Garden Records’ and try things out.

title: Tabs and split view
summary: Open documents side by side and use shortcuts
lead: In the workspace, documents and views open in tabs. Split the window in two to keep a chapter and a setting document side by side. Your tabs and layout are saved per project and come back when you reopen it.

sections.title: Work with tabs
sections.body:
- Select + at the end of the tab bar to open a new tab. A new tab offers Continue working, Create new and Recently opened.
- A document opens in only one tab per pane. If it is already open, you go to that tab.
- Drag tabs to reorder them, and close one with × or the middle mouse button. Closing the last tab leaves a new tab.
- The button at the left end of the tab bar hides and shows the sidebar.

sections.title: Split the window
sections.body:
Drag a document, or the Search, Relationship map, Timeline or Notes button, from the sidebar to an edge of the work area and a second pane opens on that side. You can also drag a tab onto the other pane's tab bar to move it there. If your writing hasn't saved yet, it saves before the tab moves.

Drag the handle between the panes to resize them. When the window is 900px wide or less, only one pane shows and the sidebar opens as a drawer.

sections.title: Keyboard shortcuts
sections.body:
- ⌘S: Save now
- ⌘F: Find and replace in the document
- ⌘⇧F: Search the project
- ⌘P: Export as PDF
- ⌘\: Show or hide the sidebar
- ⌥T: New tab, ⌥W: Close tab
- ⌃⇧] / ⌃⇧[: Next tab / previous tab
- ⌥M: Move a tab or split the window. Pick a spot with the arrow keys, press Enter to confirm or Esc to cancel.
- ⌥P: Go to the other pane

On Windows, use Ctrl for ⌘ and ⌃, and Alt for ⌥. The full list is under Keyboard shortcuts in Help.

sections.title: How your layout comes back
sections.body: Open tabs, split panes, whether the sidebar and notes panel are open, and the relationship map's category filter and episode choice are saved per project whenever they change. Opening the same project on another device starts with the same layout. The sidebar width is remembered only in this browser.

title: Files and setting documents
summary: Create setting documents and link them with properties
lead: Setting documents such as characters, places, organizations, items, events and worldbuilding have a title, a property table and a body. Relationships you link in the property table are what the relationship map, the timeline and AI chat read.

sections.title: Category folders
sections.body: Files has seven category folders: Manuscript, Character, Place, Organization, Item, Event and Worldbuilding. Every document sits in one of them, and the folder's category is the document's kind. The only folders you can create yourself are episodes inside the Manuscript folder.

sections.title: Create a document
sections.body:
Create one from any of these:

- The more menu (⋯) at the top of Files, then a category.
- A category folder's more menu, then its add item, such as Add character.
- A category under Create new on a new tab.

In the sidebar a name field appears. Type a name and press Enter to create and open the document. Press Esc or leave the name empty to cancel. If a document with that name already exists in the same folder, the notice ‘Something with this name already exists here.’ appears and nothing is created, so pick another name. Renaming works the same way.

sections.title: Move and favorite
sections.body:
Open a document's menu with its more button (⋯), a right-click or Shift+F10, then choose Add to favorites, Rename or Move to trash.

- Drag a document onto another category folder to change its category.
- Drag a document onto the Favorites heading to add it to favorites.
- The star next to a document's title also turns favorite on and off. Favorite documents get a star on their graph node and gather at the top of the timeline.

sections.title: Add properties
sections.body:
The property table under the title starts with Category and Description. A setting document can switch to another setting category from its Category row.

Select Add property to add:

- Alias: other names or short forms, as many as you like.
- Related manuscripts, Related characters, Related places, Related organizations, Related items, Related events, Related worldbuilding: link documents of that category. A relationship kind that is already there can't be added again.

sections.title: Link documents and describe the link
sections.body:
Select + on a relationship row, search for a document and pick it to add a chip. Select the chip's title to open that document, or × to unlink it. To remove the whole row, choose Delete property from the row icon's menu.

Hover over a chip and a Note button appears. Select it, describe the relationship (for example ‘mentor and student’) and press Enter; the note shows inside the chip and on the line in the relationship map. Clear the note and press Enter to remove it.

sections.title: Document image
sections.body:
Select the circle left of the title to choose an image, or drop an image file onto it. PNG, JPG, WEBP and GIF work. In the window that opens, drag the picture to frame what goes inside the circle and zoom with the wheel or the slider.

The image also shows on the document's node in the relationship map, in the selected-node list, in the timeline's name column and in search results. Select the circle again to choose Change image or Remove image.

An image isn't part of the document's content: it isn't kept in version history, and restoring a version doesn't change it. A locked document's image can't be changed.

sections.title: Check the save status
sections.body: Changes to the title, properties and body save automatically. The status at the right of the toolbar moves from Waiting to save to Saving… to Saved. If it reads Couldn't save, select Try again next to it. What you changed stays on screen.

title: Writing chapters
summary: Formatting, find, lock, export and version history
lead: A chapter is a title and a formatted body, and it saves automatically without a save button. Each document keeps its own font and line spacing, and version history lets you compare and restore earlier states.

sections.title: Group chapters into episodes
sections.body:
Choose Add episode from the Manuscript folder's more menu to create an episode folder. Add chapters to it with Add manuscript from the episode's more menu, or drag chapters onto it. You can also move a chapter from the Episode row of its property table.

Episodes set the column order of the timeline and the episode range in the relationship map.

sections.title: Import an existing manuscript
sections.body:
Select Import in the sidebar or on a new tab, then Choose files or drag files into the window. You can add several plain text (.txt) and Markdown (.md) files at once.

- Check the files in the list and take out any you don't want.
- Nothing is created until you select Import.
- Each file name becomes a chapter title. Markdown keeps formatting such as headings and lists; plain text becomes one paragraph per line.

sections.title: Fonts and formatting
sections.body:
The toolbar's font, font size and line spacing apply only to the open document and are saved with it. Other documents keep their own look, so chapters and setting documents can use different fonts. ⌘Z undoes a formatting change too.

- Fonts: Pretendard (default), Nanum Gothic, Nanum Myeongjo, Noto Serif KR and Mono. Fonts installed on this device (Malgun Gothic, Batang and others) look the same only on devices that have them.
- Font size is 10–16pt (default 10.5pt) and line spacing is 1.5–2 (default 1.5).
- Bold ⌘B, italic ⌘I, underline ⌘U, strikethrough ⌘⇧S, bulleted list ⌘⇧8, numbered list ⌘⇧7
- Inside a list, Tab indents and Shift+Tab outdents.

Alignment (⌘⇧L, E, R, J) applies to the whole document when nothing is selected, or only to the selected paragraphs. When the window is narrow, less-used tools move into the more menu (⋯).

sections.title: Find and replace
sections.body:
Press ⌘F or select Find and replace in the toolbar to open the find bar above the body. Type what to find and every match is marked, with a count of where you are. Enter goes to the next match and Shift+Enter to the previous one.

Type a replacement and select Replace or Replace all to fix a repeated phrase in one go. Matching ignores case, and Esc closes the bar.

sections.title: Character count
sections.body: The toolbar shows the character count with spaces and without spaces. Only the body is counted, not the title.

sections.title: When it was changed elsewhere
sections.body: If the same document was edited in another tab or on another device, changes to different paragraphs are merged automatically when it saves. Only when both sides changed the same paragraph does a notice appear, and you choose Keep my changes or Load the latest version.

sections.title: Lock a document
sections.body:
Select Lock in the file tools to save any remaining changes and lock the document. A locked document's title, body, properties and formatting can't be changed, and versions can't be saved or restored. Use it to keep a finished chapter from accidental edits. Select Unlock to edit again.

Documents a setting document refresh reads are locked too. That lock is lifted only when you confirm the refresh results or the refresh fails, and Unlock can't lift it. A note above the editor says so.

sections.title: Export
sections.body:
Choose a format from Export in the file tools. Any remaining changes save first.

- PDF (⌘P): when the browser's print dialog opens, choose Save as PDF as the destination. The title, properties and body print in the document's font.
- Markdown (.md): the title, category, properties and formatted body.
- Plain text (.txt): the title and the body without formatting.

Microsoft Word (.docx) and Hangul (.hwp) are coming soon. Paragraph alignment isn't kept in Markdown or plain text.

sections.title: Version history
sections.body:
Select Version history in the file tools. Pick a version on the left to compare it side by side with the current document.

- Save version keeps the current state as a version.
- Restore this version goes back to the selected version. The state just before restoring is kept as a Before restore version, so a restore can be undone too.

Versions are labeled with how they were made, such as Autosave, Saved manually, Before restore or From refresh. If an edit couldn't be saved, save it before restoring.

title: Search and relationship map
summary: Find anything in the project and explore relationships
lead: Search finds text in the titles and bodies of your chapters and setting documents, and the relationship map shows the relationships you linked in property tables.

sections.title: Search documents
sections.body:
Select Search at the top of the sidebar or press ⌘⇧F. Results appear shortly after you type, with the matching text marked in soft teal.

- Each result shows its category, episode, when it was last edited and whether it is locked or a favorite.
- Sort by Best match, Recently edited or Title above the list, and flip the order with the Descending/Ascending button next to them. Best match and Recently edited start descending; Title starts ascending (A to Z).
- Best match has three tiers: documents whose title is exactly the search, then documents whose title contains it, then documents where only the body does. Within a tier, the most recently edited comes first.
- Enter opens the first result. ↓ moves into the results, ↑↓ moves between them and Esc clears the search.

Documents in the trash aren't searched. Only the first 50 results show, so make the search more specific if there are too many. Words aren't split, so searching for ‘Lena's’ finds only places where that exact text appears.

sections.title: Explore the relationship map
sections.body:
Nodes are documents and lines are the relationships linked in property tables. A document with more relationships has a bigger node, and favorite documents carry a star at the top right of their node.

Selecting a node highlights the documents directly connected to it, and the Selected node panel on the right describes it and its neighbors. Select a card in the panel to open that document. Select more nodes to highlight each one's connections together, or select an empty spot to clear the selection. The words on a line are the note you wrote for that relationship in the property table.

Use the zoom buttons to change the scale and Fit to screen to see everything again.

sections.title: Find a node
sections.body: Select Find a node and type a name to see up to 8 matching nodes. Names that start with what you typed come first, then nodes with more relationships. Pick one and it becomes the only selected node and moves to the center.

sections.title: Filters and episodes
sections.body:
Keep only the categories you want with Category filter, and choose an episode range from the Episode menu to keep only the nodes directly connected to those chapters. You can pick several episodes. The filter and episodes you chose stay the same next time.

When there are more than 150 nodes, only manuscripts, characters and events show at first; select Show all in the banner to turn everything on.

title: Setting document refresh
summary: Review and apply what's new in your chapters
lead: Setting document refresh has AI read the chapters and setting documents you changed and propose details and relationships to add to your setting documents. Nothing changes until you review the proposals and confirm them, and every applied document is kept in its version history.

sections.title: Start a refresh
sections.body:
Select Refresh setting docs in the sidebar and confirm with Start refresh. What you're writing is saved, the chapters and setting documents changed since the last refresh are sent, and the item changes to Refreshing docs… with the time waited so far. The documents sent stay locked until you confirm the results, so they can't be edited, renamed, moved or trashed.

A refresh can take a few minutes. It keeps going if you switch views or browsers, and when it finishes you're notified and the item changes to Apply changes. Nothing starts if no document changed. If no result comes within an hour or the refresh fails, you're notified and the locks are lifted.

sections.title: Review the proposals
sections.body:
The list on the left shows each document that would change, marked modified (~) or added (+). Documents changed after the AI read them are marked as such. Pick one to see Current and Proposed side by side with the differences marked.

- The arrow on each row copies that value to the other side. The Whole document arrow copies the entire document.
- You can edit the title, properties, relationships and body directly on either side.
- Use current keeps the document as it is, and Use proposed accepts the proposal. Reset returns that document to where it started.

When both sides match, the document is settled and gets a check in the list.

sections.title: Apply the changes
sections.body:
Apply changes turns on once every document is settled. What gets applied is the state both sides agree on. A proposed new document is created when you bring it to the left, and isn't created if you remove it from the right.

Each applied document gets a From refresh version in its history, and confirming lifts every lock. If something can't be applied as it is, such as a relationship to a new document you chose not to create, you're told what's wrong and nothing is applied.

sections.title: Finish later
sections.body: Your choices are saved as you go. Close the review or open it in another browser or device, and select Apply changes in the sidebar to pick up where you left off. A new refresh can't start until you confirm the review.

title: Notes and timeline
summary: Jot down ideas and see where each document appears
lead: Notes are working notes attached to the whole story or to one document. The timeline is a table of which chapters each setting document appears in.

sections.title: Story notes
sections.body:
Open Notes in the sidebar, choose Story notes and select Add note. Keep as many notes about the whole story, ideas or to-dos as you like.

Choose Document notes to see the notes left on each document, grouped by document; select a document's name to open it.

sections.title: The notes panel beside a document
sections.body:
Select Notes in a document's file tools to open the notes panel beside it. Switch between this document's notes and story notes with the tabs at the top, and select + to write a new note.

- Choose Right or Bottom under Notes position.
- Drag the panel's edge to resize it.
- If the panel is on the right and the editing area gets narrow, the panel folds away. Select Reopen to bring it back docked at the bottom.

sections.title: Save a note
sections.body:
Notes don't save automatically. Write freely, and when you want to keep it select Save or press ⌘Enter (Ctrl+Enter on Windows). Cancel or Esc discards your changes.

Select a saved note's card to edit it in place, or its × to delete it. Deleted notes can't be recovered.

sections.title: Read the timeline
sections.body:
Columns are chapters, in episode order. Rows are setting documents grouped by category folder, with favorites gathered at the top. A filled bar marks a chapter the document appears in: one linked to that chapter through a property-table relationship.

- Select a chapter heading once to select its column, twice to open the chapter.
- Select a row's name to open that document.
- Choose which chapters to show from the Episode menu and which rows from Rows to show.

title: AI chat
summary: Ask about your story and see where each answer comes from
lead: AI chat reads your chapters, setting documents, the relationships between them and your notes all at once, then answers your question. It only answers and never edits your manuscript.

sections.title: Open the chat
sections.body: Press the round button at the bottom right of the workspace to open the chat window. You can keep writing while it's open. Drag its left or top edge, or its top-left corner, to resize it, and double-click an edge to go back to the default size. This browser remembers the size you choose.

sections.title: Ask a question
sections.body: Type a question on the first screen, or pick a suggested one, to start a new conversation. The answer appears once the whole story has been read, and while you wait you can see what it's doing and how long it has taken.

sections.title: Ask about a passage
sections.body: Select a passage in a document's text and a small bar appears. Choose Ask AI to add the passage to the question box as a quote, or choose Explain, Related settings or Before and after to ask right away. If a conversation is open in the chat window, the question goes there. Otherwise a new conversation starts.

sections.title: Read answers and sources
sections.body: Each source appears as a chip with the document's name, colored by document type. Notes are your working notes, so they're kept apart from chapter and setting sources as gray note chips. Hover over a chip to see the quoted text, and click it to open the document or your notes. Use the copy button under an answer to copy it.

sections.title: Stop and ask again
sections.body: While an answer is being written, press the stop button in the question box. Unfinished answers aren't kept, and Ask again sends the same question once more. Hover over your last question and click the pencil to edit it and get a new answer.

sections.title: Search and manage conversations
sections.body: Search conversations on the first screen to look through their titles and what was said. Matches are highlighted, and Enter opens the first result. Use the ⋯ menu at the top of a conversation to rename or delete it. A deleted conversation can't be restored.

sections.title: When a story is too long
sections.body: If your chapters, settings and notes together are more than AI chat can read at once, the chat button turns gray. Click it to see how long the story is and what the limit is.

title: AI setting check
summary: Find where a chapter contradicts your settings or earlier chapters
lead: Setting check takes one chapter and has the AI look for sentences that seem to contradict your setting documents or the facts of earlier chapters. The result is a list of mismatches. You judge each one as ‘Intended’ or ‘Not a conflict’, and the next check reads those verdicts. The AI never edits your manuscript.

sections.title: Starting a check
sections.body:
Press ‘Setting check’ in the sidebar to open the check screen. Pick the chapter at the top, press ‘Start check’, then confirm in the dialog. With no chapters in the project the screen says there is nothing to check and the button stays off.

A check usually takes 1–3 minutes and you can keep writing elsewhere. While it runs you see the stages ‘Reading earlier chapters and settings’ and ‘Looking for mismatches’. A new check on the same chapter cannot start until the running one finishes.

sections.title: What it reads
sections.body:
It reads the chosen chapter, the chapters before it and the setting documents. Paragraphs you marked as ‘core setting’ in a setting document count as facts that must hold and are compared first. When an earlier chapter and a setting document disagree, that is reported too.

If you edit the chapter after a check, the result shows ‘The chapter changed after this check’ and ‘Check again’ gives you a fresh result.

sections.title: Marking core settings
sections.body: Select a paragraph in a setting document’s body and press ‘Mark as core setting’ in the small bar that appears. Marked paragraphs are counted in the ‘Core settings’ row of the property table, and ‘Unmark’ in the same bar removes the mark. Checks work without any marks, but marking the facts that matter makes mismatches more precise.

sections.title: Reading and judging mismatches
sections.body:
The result pairs each suspicious sentence of the chapter with the sentence of the setting document or earlier chapter it clashes with. ‘View in {title}’ jumps to that sentence. Items the AI is unsure about carry ‘Low confidence’.

Each item takes one of three verdicts.

- To check: not reviewed yet. Fix the chapter or change the setting.
- Intended: you wrote it that way on purpose. Write the reason and the next check reads it instead of raising the same place again.
- Not a conflict: the AI misread it. The reason you write is used by the next check.

Verdicts save immediately and ‘Undo’ returns an item to ‘To check’. When nothing clashes, the result says every fact in the setting documents was kept.

sections.title: Past checks and verdicts
sections.body: ‘Past checks’ at the bottom of the screen lists each chapter’s result: the number of mismatches, none, or a failed check. ‘Verdict log’ shows every ‘Intended’ and ‘Not a conflict’ verdict in one place, where you can undo them. The sidebar item shows how many mismatches are still ‘To check’.

title: Trash and restore
summary: Bring items back or delete them for good
lead: Deleted documents go to the workspace trash and deleted projects go to the trash in your project list. From the trash you can restore them to where they were, or delete them permanently after confirming.

sections.title: Move to trash
sections.body: Move a document with Move to trash in its sidebar menu. Move a project from its card menu or from the Danger zone in project settings. Moving a document closes any tabs it was open in.

sections.title: Restore
sections.body:
Open Trash at the bottom of the workspace sidebar to see deleted documents with their original path and when they were deleted. Select Restore to put one back where it was, and Open in the notification to open it straight away.

Restore projects from Trash on the left of your project list.

sections.title: Delete permanently
sections.body: Select Delete permanently and confirm to remove an item for good; it can't be restored. Deleting a project permanently removes all of its files and settings with it.

sections.title: Delete an episode folder
sections.body: Episode folders don't go to the trash. Choose Delete episode folder from an episode's more menu and only the folder goes; the chapters in it return to the Manuscript folder.

title: Settings and account
summary: Project details, theme, language and your account
lead: Change a project's name and description in the workspace's Settings, and your display name, language and theme from the account menu.

sections.title: Project settings
sections.body: Change the project's name and description under Settings at the bottom of the workspace sidebar. When you change something, Cancel and Save changes appear below; your edits save only when you select Save changes. If you try to close the tab without saving, you're asked whether to discard them.

sections.title: Theme and language
sections.body: Choose Use system setting, Dark or Light under Theme in the account menu at the top left. To change the language, pick Korean or English under Language in Account settings; it switches right away.

sections.title: Account settings
sections.body: Change your display name in Account settings from the account menu. Your email comes from the Google account you signed in with and can't be changed.

sections.title: Delete your account
sections.body: Select Delete account under Account settings. You're asked why you're leaving (answering is optional) and shown what will be deleted. Type your account email exactly to confirm. All projects and trash items are deleted permanently and can't be recovered.

sections.title: Send feedback
sections.body: Write to us from Send feedback in your project list or under Help in the workspace. ⌘Enter (Ctrl+Enter on Windows) sends it too.
